summary: British rule over India ends with the subcontinent divided into two independent states: India, with a Hindu majority, and Pakistan, with a Muslim majority, in two parts in the west and east. Hastily drawn borders through Punjab and Bengal set off mass violence and one of the largest migrations in history, as an estimated 10 to 20 million people cross them. Estimates of the dead range from about 200,000 to two million.
significance: India became the world's largest democracy, while Partition left a lasting hostility between India and Pakistan, including the unresolved dispute over Kashmir.

title: Postwar Japan
summary: Under American occupation Japan adopted a new constitution in 1947 that made the emperor a symbol, gave power to an elected parliament and renounced war. Independent again from 1952 and allied with the United States, it rebuilt its industry and by 1968 had the second-largest economy in the world.
significance: Japan's recovery from total defeat to prosperity as a peaceful democracy was a model for the rest of East Asia.

title: State of Israel founded
summary: As the British Mandate for Palestine ends, Jewish leaders headed by David Ben-Gurion declare the State of Israel in Tel Aviv, following a 1947 UN plan to divide Palestine into Jewish and Arab states. After months of fighting between Jewish and Arab forces, neighboring Arab states send armies in, and by the end of the war Israel holds more territory than the UN plan proposed, while about 700,000 Palestinian Arabs have fled or been expelled from their homes, an event Palestinians call the Nakba (catastrophe).
significance: Israel became a refuge for Jews from Europe after the Holocaust and from across the Middle East, while the unresolved conflict between Israelis, Palestinians and Arab states has shaped the region's politics ever since.

title: North Korea
summary: The Democratic People's Republic of Korea was founded in the Soviet zone of occupation under Kim Il Sung, who invaded the South in 1950. After the war he built a closed, heavily armed state around his own rule and passed power to his son Kim Jong Il in 1994, as the loss of Soviet aid and a famine devastated the country.
significance: It is the world's most isolated state and the only communist one to become a hereditary dynasty.

title: South Korea
summary: The Republic of Korea was founded in the American zone of occupation and was left among the poorest countries in the world by the Korean War. Under military-backed governments from 1961 it industrialized at great speed through export manufacturing, and after mass protests in 1987 it became a democracy.
significance: Its rise from poverty to wealth and democracy within two generations is one of the most striking transformations of the 20th century.

title: People's Republic of China founded
summary: As the Communists win the civil war against Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalists, whose government retreats to Taiwan by the end of the year, Mao Zedong proclaims the People's Republic of China from Tiananmen Gate in Beijing. The Chinese Communist Party takes control of mainland China.
significance: Communist rule unified China under a strong central state, and after the upheavals of the Mao years it became, from the 1980s, one of the world's fastest-growing economies and a major global power.

title: People's Republic of China
summary: The People's Republic was proclaimed in 1949 after the Communist victory in the civil war. Under Mao Zedong it collectivized the economy and went through the Great Leap Forward and the Cultural Revolution; reforms begun under Deng Xiaoping in 1978 opened it to markets and trade.
significance: It united mainland China under one government and, after the reforms, grew into one of the world's largest economies and a major global power.

title: Taiwan (Republic of China)
summary: After losing the civil war, Chiang Kai-shek's Nationalist government moved to Taiwan with about two million soldiers and refugees and ruled under martial law until 1987. The island industrialized rapidly, lost China's seat at the United Nations to Beijing in 1971, and held its first direct presidential election in 1996.
significance: Taiwan became a prosperous democracy whose status remains one of the most dangerous unresolved disputes in world politics.

title: Korean War
summary: War between North and South Korea drew in United Nations forces, led by the United States, and China. The 1953 armistice ended major fighting but left the peninsula divided without a peace treaty.
significance: It fixed the division of Korea into two hostile states and turned the Cold War into a global military confrontation.

title: Structure of DNA discovered
summary: At the University of Cambridge, James Watson and Francis Crick propose that DNA is a double helix: two strands wound around each other and joined by pairs of chemical bases. Their model relies heavily on X-ray images and data from Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins at King's College London, notably an image from Franklin's lab known as Photo 51.
significance: The structure showed how genetic information is stored and copied, opening the way to molecular biology, genetic engineering and DNA sequencing.

title: Japanese economic miracle
summary: For nearly two decades Japan's economy grew by about ten percent a year. Close cooperation between government and business, high savings, new technology and exports of steel, ships, cars and electronics made it the second-largest economy in the world by 1968. The oil shock of 1973 brought the fastest growth to an end.
significance: Japan's export-led growth was the model later followed by South Korea, Taiwan and China.

title: Vietnam War
summary: After the French defeat in 1954, Vietnam is divided into a communist North and a US-backed South, and communist-led insurgents, supported by the North, fight the southern government. From 1965 the United States sends hundreds of thousands of troops, while the Soviet Union and China supply the North. US forces withdraw in 1973, and North Vietnamese forces take Saigon in April 1975, reuniting the country.
significance: Estimates of the dead range from about one million to over three million, most of them Vietnamese, along with more than 58,000 Americans; the war also spread into Laos and Cambodia and deeply divided American society.

title: Ghana's independence leads African decolonization
summary: The British colony of the Gold Coast becomes independent as Ghana, led by Kwame Nkrumah, after a decade of nationalist campaigning. It is one of the first colonies in sub-Saharan Africa to win independence, following Sudan in 1956.
significance: Ghana's independence inspired anti-colonial movements across the continent, and by the late 1960s most of Africa's former colonies had become independent states.

title: Sputnik, the first satellite
summary: The Soviet Union launches Sputnik 1, a 58-centimeter metal ball with four long antennas, from a launch site in what is now Kazakhstan, putting the first artificial satellite into orbit around the Earth. Its radio beeps can be picked up by listeners around the world.
significance: Sputnik shocked the United States and started the space race, leading to the creation of NASA, heavy investment in science education and, in 1969, the Moon landing.

title: Great Leap Forward

location.name: Beijing (representative; the famine was worst in inland provinces)

summary: Mao Zedong launches a campaign to overtake the industrial powers within years. Farmers are organized into huge communes and millions are set to making steel in backyard furnaces, while officials report harvests that do not exist and the state takes grain on that basis. The result is the deadliest famine in recorded history.
significance: Estimates of the deaths range from about 15 million to 45 million or more; the disaster weakened Mao's position and led him to launch the Cultural Revolution to regain it.

title: Cuban Missile Crisis

location.name: Havana (representative; the missile sites were across western Cuba)

summary: US spy planes discover that the Soviet Union is secretly installing nuclear missiles in Cuba, about 150 km from Florida, and President John F. Kennedy orders a naval blockade, called a quarantine, of the island. For thirteen days the world faces the risk of nuclear war, until Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev agrees to remove the missiles in return for a US pledge not to invade Cuba and a secret promise to withdraw US missiles from Turkey.
significance: It is often seen as the closest the Cold War came to nuclear war, and afterward the superpowers set up a direct hotline and signed a treaty limiting nuclear tests.

title: First bullet train
summary: Japan opens the Tokaido Shinkansen between Tokyo and Osaka, with trains running at up to 210 kilometers an hour on a dedicated line. It opens nine days before the Tokyo Olympics, the first held in Asia.
significance: It was the world's first high-speed railway and, with the Olympics, announced Japan's return as an advanced nation.

title: Cultural Revolution
summary: Mao Zedong launches the Cultural Revolution to purge rivals and what he calls bourgeois and traditional elements from Chinese society. Young Red Guards attack teachers, officials and intellectuals and destroy temples and historical relics, and millions of urban youths are later sent to the countryside; the movement ends with Mao's death in 1976.
significance: Estimates of the dead range from hundreds of thousands to about two million or more, and the chaos discredited radical Maoism and helped open the way for Deng Xiaoping's reforms.

title: Apollo 11 Moon landing
summary: NASA's Apollo 11 mission lands Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin on the Moon while Michael Collins orbits above. The two astronauts spend about two and a half hours walking on the lunar surface before returning safely to Earth.
significance: It was the first time humans set foot on another world, and the high point of the Cold War space race between the United States and the Soviet Union.

title: Nixon visits China
summary: Richard Nixon becomes the first American president to visit the People's Republic of China, meeting Mao Zedong and Zhou Enlai after more than twenty years in which the two countries had no relations. In a joint statement issued in Shanghai, both sides agree to work toward normal relations and set out their differences over Taiwan.
significance: The opening shifted the balance of the Cold War against the Soviet Union and prepared the way for China's later entry into the world economy.

title: Deng Xiaoping's economic reforms
summary: Two years after Mao's death, Deng Xiaoping becomes China's leading figure and, at a Communist Party meeting in December 1978, launches a policy of 'reform and opening up'. Farmers are allowed to sell surplus crops for profit, private businesses are gradually permitted, and special economic zones such as Shenzhen open to foreign investment.
significance: The reforms began decades of very rapid growth that lifted hundreds of millions of people out of poverty and made China a leading industrial and trading power, while the Communist Party kept its monopoly on political power.

title: Iranian Revolution
summary: After a year of mass protests and strikes against Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi, the shah leaves Iran and the exiled cleric Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini returns to a huge welcome. His supporters take power, and a referendum makes Iran an Islamic Republic, with Khomeini as Supreme Leader.
significance: The revolution created a state ruled by Shia clergy, turned Iran from a US ally into an opponent, and inspired Islamist political movements across the Muslim world.

title: South Korea's June Democratic Struggle
summary: After a student dies under police torture and the military-backed president names his successor, millions of South Koreans take to the streets for nearly three weeks. On 29 June the government gives way and accepts direct presidential elections and the restoration of civil rights.
significance: The protests ended decades of authoritarian rule; South Korea has been a democracy since.

title: Fall of the Berlin Wall
summary: As protests and mass emigration shake communist East Germany, its government announces that citizens may cross the border, and crowds pour through the checkpoints of the Berlin Wall, which has divided the city since 1961. Germans from both sides climb on the wall and begin chipping it apart.
significance: The fall of the wall became the symbol of the end of communist rule in Eastern Europe and of the Cold War division of Europe, and Germany was reunified in October 1990.

title: Tiananmen Square protests
summary: Students occupying Tiananmen Square in Beijing to call for political reform and an end to corruption are joined by workers and residents, and protests spread to other cities. On the night of 3 to 4 June the army clears the streets around the square with tanks and gunfire. Estimates of the dead range from several hundred to several thousand.
significance: The crackdown ended hopes of political liberalization alongside China's economic reforms, and discussion of it remains censored in China.

title: Dissolution of the Soviet Union
summary: After a failed coup by communist hardliners in August 1991, the Soviet republics declare independence one after another. Mikhail Gorbachev resigns as Soviet president on 25 December, and the Soviet Union is formally dissolved the next day, splitting into fifteen independent countries, the largest of them Russia.
significance: It marked the end of the Cold War and left the United States as the sole superpower, while the former Soviet states went through hard economic and political transitions.

title: World Wide Web goes public
summary: Tim Berners-Lee, a British scientist at CERN, the European physics laboratory near Geneva, makes his World Wide Web system available to the public over the internet. Proposed in 1989, it links documents on different computers through hyperlinks, using web addresses (URLs), the HTML page format and the HTTP protocol.
significance: After CERN put the technology in the public domain in 1993, the web grew explosively and became the main way people use the internet, transforming communication, commerce and access to information.

title: End of apartheid in South Africa
summary: South Africa holds its first elections in which citizens of all races can vote, ending apartheid, the system of racial segregation and white minority rule in force since 1948. Nelson Mandela, released in 1990 after 27 years in prison, leads the African National Congress to victory and is inaugurated as president in Pretoria.
significance: The largely peaceful transfer of power, followed by a Truth and Reconciliation Commission, made South Africa a constitutional democracy, though deep economic inequality remained.

title: Rwandan genocide
summary: After the plane carrying Rwanda's Hutu president Juvénal Habyarimana is shot down, Hutu extremist militias and soldiers begin killing Tutsi and moderate Hutu across the country. In about 100 days an estimated 500,000 to 800,000 people, most of them Tutsi, are murdered, many with machetes, until the Tutsi-led Rwandan Patriotic Front defeats the government forces.
significance: The genocide, which the UN and Western powers failed to stop, led to an international tribunal and the doctrine of a 'responsibility to protect', and its aftermath fed wars in neighboring Congo.

title: Hong Kong returns to China
summary: At midnight, Britain hands Hong Kong to China after more than 150 years of colonial rule, as the lease on most of its territory expires. Under an arrangement called one country, two systems, China promises that the city will keep its own laws, courts and economic system for fifty years.
significance: The handover marked the end of the British Empire in Asia and, for China, the closing of the era that began with the Opium War.
